overview: A servo bracket is a small precision-cut mounting piece shaped to hold a standard-size hobby servo securely while exposing its horn for attaching the next link in a chain — stack several of these (a 'U-bracket' for a joint, an 'L-bracket' for a perpendicular turn) and you can build a multi-jointed robotic arm without any custom fabrication. Buying a matched kit avoids the single most common beginner robotic-arm mistake: mounting holes and servo horn spacing that don't quite line up between differently-sourced brackets, causing wobble or bind at every joint.
simpleSummary: Precision-cut mounting pieces that let you bolt several servos together into a robotic arm.

specifications.material: Laser-cut acrylic, 3D-printed plastic, or CNC-cut aluminum
specifications.servoCompatibility: Sized for standard servos (SG90-class) or larger (MG996R-class), rarely both without adapters
specifications.bracketTypes: U-bracket (dual-support joint), L-bracket (perpendicular mount), straight extension links
specifications.degreesOfFreedom: A typical small arm kit provides 4-6 DOF (base rotation, shoulder, elbow, wrist, gripper)

pinMap.name: Servo Mounting Holes
pinMap.function: Screw holes matched to a specific servo size's mounting tab pattern.
pinMap.gotcha: Mixing bracket sets designed for different servo sizes (e.g. SG90 vs MG996R patterns) is the most common reason a kit's parts don't quite fit together.

pinMap.name: Horn Attachment Point
pinMap.function: Where the servo's rotating horn attaches to the next link, transferring the servo's rotation into arm movement.

pinMap.name: Joint Bearing/Idler
pinMap.function: On U-bracket joints, a free-spinning support point opposite the servo horn, preventing the joint from wobbling under load.
pinMap.gotcha: Skipping the idler-side support (mounting a joint on the servo horn alone) is a common cause of a sagging, imprecise arm under any real payload.

useCases.title: Desktop pick-and-place robotic arm
useCases.scenario: A 4-6 DOF arm for picking up and moving small objects, the classic servo-based robotics teaching project.

useCases.title: Camera pan-tilt-roll mount
useCases.scenario: Multi-axis camera stabilization or aiming mechanism.

oftenConfusedWith: Aluminum extrusion framing (general structural framing, not servo-specific)
oftenUpgradedTo: Metal-geared, higher-precision arm kits or fully custom CNC-machined arm structures
